subject: Architecture
title: The Morandi Bridge: Genoa's Tragedy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Morandi Bridge: Genoa's Tragedy.

hook.text: In August 2018, a section of Genoa's Morandi Bridge collapsed during a storm, killing 43 people.

buildup.text: The bridge used a unique cable-stayed design with concrete-encased cables — impossible to inspect visually.

discovery.text: Corrosion had weakened the cables inside their concrete shells for decades without anyone seeing the damage.

twist.text: Italy's bridge infrastructure crisis was well known. Budget cuts had delayed maintenance for years.

climax.text: Renzo Piano designed the replacement — a sleek, inspectable steel bridge built in record time.

punchline.text: Concrete hid the cables. It also hid the failure waiting inside.

quiz.question: Why couldn't inspectors detect the Morandi Bridge's cable corrosion?
options: The cables were too high to reach safely
Concrete encasement hid the cables from visual inspection
Digital sensors were never installed on the bridge

details.summary: The Morandi Bridge in Genoa, Italy, collapsed on August 14, 2018, killing 43 people. A section of the cable-stayed concrete viaduct failed catastrophically during a rainstorm, dropping vehicles 45 meters.
details.whyItMatters: The Morandi collapse forced global reassessment of aging infrastructure. It demonstrated that structurally innovative bridges require corresponding maintenance innovation, and that ignoring deterioration warnings can be deadly.
takeaways: Collapsed August 14, 2018, killing 43 people in Genoa
Systemic failures in maintenance and inspection were exposed
It triggered worldwide reassessment of aging bridge infrastructure

faq.question: What caused the Morandi Bridge to collapse?
faq.answer: Corrosion of the stay cables and their concrete encasement weakened the structure over decades. Engineer Riccardo Morandi's unusual design encased steel cables in concrete, making inspection nearly impossible. Warning signs of deterioration were documented but not adequately acted upon.

faq.question: What happened after the collapse?
faq.answer: The remaining bridge was demolished and replaced with the Genova San Giorgio Bridge, designed by Renzo Piano, in just 20 months. Criminal proceedings were initiated against bridge managers and inspectors. Italy launched a national infrastructure assessment program for aging bridges.
